🎬 Bicentennial Man (1999)

Bicentennial Man follows Andrew Martin, an extraordinary household robot purchased by the Martin family to help with everyday tasks. Unlike other robots, Andrew gradually begins developing emotions, creativity, curiosity, and a unique personality that makes him increasingly different from the machines around him. As the years pass, he forms a deep connection with the Martin family, especially their youngest daughter, Little Miss, who recognizes his unusual ability to understand human feelings. Determined to discover what it truly means to be human, Andrew begins a remarkable journey spanning two centuries, during which he pursues independence, develops artistic talents, experiences love, and searches for acceptance in a world that considers him nothing more than a machine. Along the way, he faces heartbreaking losses, extraordinary discoveries, and difficult choices that challenge the boundaries between humanity and artificial intelligence. Starring Robin Williams, Embeth Davidtz, Sam Neill, Oliver Platt, and Wendy Crewson, the film delivers a beautiful and emotional story about love, family, identity, mortality, acceptance, and the extraordinary desire to belong.

🎭 Genre: Science Fiction • Drama • Romance • Fantasy

⭐ IMDb: 6.9/10

⏱️ Runtime: 2h 12m • PG

🎥 Director: Chris Columbus

✍️ Writer: Nicholas Kazan

📚 Based On: Isaac Asimov’s 1976 short story The Bicentennial Man and the novel The Positronic Man, written by Isaac Asimov and Robert Silverberg.

🤖 Themes: Artificial intelligence, humanity, love, freedom, identity, and the meaning of life.

🏆 Awards: Nominated for the Academy Award for Best Makeup.

📺 Where to Watch: Check Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV, and Fandango at Home for current streaming, rental, or purchase availability in the United States.

source_details.synopsis: Bicentennial Man is a 1999 American science fiction comedy drama film, directed by Chris Columbus, and starring Robin Williams, Sam Neill, Embeth Davidtz, Wendy Crewson and Oliver Platt. Based on the 1976 novelette of the same name by Isaac Asimov and the 1992 novel The Positronic Man by Asimov and Robert Silverberg, the title derives from the main character existing to the age of two hundred years. Bicentennial Man was released in the United States on December 17, 1999, by Buena Vista Pictures Distribution under the Touchstone Pictures banner, with Columbia TriStar Film Distributors International releasing in other territories under the Columbia Pictures banner.
